constexpr int HEAD_K_DIM    = SSM_D_STATE;                // 128
constexpr int CONV_CHANNELS = SSM_D_INNER + 2 * SSM_N_GROUP * SSM_D_STATE; // 6144 + 2*16*128 = 10240

constexpr float EPS         = 1e-6f;
constexpr float ROPE_THETA  = 10000000.0f;
}  // namespace q35

// ─── TargetCache allocation ─────────────────────────────────────────

bool create_target_cache(const TargetWeights & w,
                         int max_ctx,
                         int max_verify_tokens,
                         ggml_backend_t backend,
                         TargetCache & out,
                         bool prefill_only) {
    return create_target_cache_partial(w, max_ctx, max_verify_tokens, backend,
                                       out, prefill_only,
                                       0, w.n_layer, true);
}

bool create_target_cache_partial(const TargetWeights & w,
                                 int max_ctx,
                                 int max_verify_tokens,
                                 ggml_backend_t backend,
                                 TargetCache & out,
                                 bool prefill_only,
                                 int layer_begin,
                                 int layer_end,
                                 bool allocate_target_feat) {
    if (layer_begin < 0) layer_begin = 0;
    if (layer_end < 0 || layer_end > w.n_layer) layer_end = w.n_layer;
    if (layer_begin > layer_end) {
        set_last_error("invalid target cache layer range");
        return false;
    }
    out.backend = backend;
    out.max_ctx = max_ctx;
    out.cur_pos = 0;
    if (max_verify_tokens <= 0) {
        max_verify_tokens = DFLASH27B_DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE;
    }

    const int n_full_attn = w.n_layer / w.full_attention_interval; // 16
    const int n_delta     = w.n_layer - n_full_attn;               // 48
    const int head_dim    = w.n_embd_head_k;
    const int head_v_dim  = w.ssm_d_inner / w.ssm_dt_rank;
    const int conv_ch     = w.ssm_d_inner + 2 * w.ssm_n_group * w.ssm_d_state;

    out.attn_k.assign(n_full_attn, nullptr);
    out.attn_v.assign(n_full_attn, nullptr);
    out.ssm_state.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_state.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.ssm_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.ssm_intermediate.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_input_cache.assign(n_delta, nullptr);

    // KV cache element types (resolved from env; aborts on unsupported pair).
    ggml_type kv_k_type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0;
    ggml_type kv_v_type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0;
    dflash::resolve_kv_types(kv_k_type, kv_v_type);
    out.kv_k_type = kv_k_type;
    out.kv_v_type = kv_v_type;

    // Graph-level FWHT K-rotation (TurboQuant-style outlier spreading with
    // standard quant types that keep fast FA kernel paths on all arches).
    // Skip for TQ3_0 K cache — that type already applies WHT during quantization.
    out.kv_k_rotated = (kv_k_type != GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0);

    const bool needs_256_stride =
        kv_k_type == GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0 || kv_v_type == GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0;
    const int max_ctx_alloc = needs_256_stride
        ? ((max_ctx + 255) / 256) * 256
        : max_ctx;

    // ── Base context: KV cache + SSM/conv state + target_feat ────────
    {
        const int base_tensors = 2 * n_full_attn + 2 * n_delta + 1;
        ggml_init_params ip{};
        ip.mem_size   = (size_t)(base_tensors + 16) * ggml_tensor_overhead();
        ip.mem_buffer = nullptr;
        ip.no_alloc   = true;
        out.base_ctx = ggml_init(ip);
        if (!out.base_ctx) { set_last_error("base cache ggml_init failed"); return false; }

        int fa_idx = 0, dn_idx = 0;
        for (int il = 0; il < w.n_layer; il++) {
            const bool is_attn = (((il + 1) % w.full_attention_interval) == 0);
            const bool owns_layer = il >= layer_begin && il < layer_end;
            if (is_attn) {
                if (!owns_layer) { fa_idx++; continue; }
                // [head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, n_head_kv]
                ggml_tensor * K = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, kv_k_type,
                                                     head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, w.n_head_kv);
                ggml_tensor * V = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, kv_v_type,
                                                     head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, w.n_head_kv);
                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "cache_k_%d", il);
                ggml_set_name(K, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "cache_v_%d", il);
                ggml_set_name(V, name);
                out.attn_k[fa_idx] = K;
                out.attn_v[fa_idx] = V;
                fa_idx++;
            } else {
                if (!owns_layer) { dn_idx++; continue; }
                // ssm_state: [head_v_dim, head_v_dim, num_v_heads]
                ggml_tensor * S = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                     head_v_dim, head_v_dim, w.ssm_dt_rank);
                // conv_state: [kernel-1, conv_channels]
                ggml_tensor * C = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                     w.ssm_d_conv - 1, conv_ch);
                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_state_%d", il);  ggml_set_name(S, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_state_%d", il); ggml_set_name(C, name);
                out.ssm_state[dn_idx]  = S;
                out.conv_state[dn_idx] = C;
                dn_idx++;
            }
        }

        constexpr int TARGET_FEAT_CAP_DEFAULT = 4096;
        out.target_feat_cap = std::min(max_ctx, TARGET_FEAT_CAP_DEFAULT);
        if (allocate_target_feat) {
            const int feat_per_cap = (out.feat_dim_per_capture > 0)
                ? out.feat_dim_per_capture : (int)w.n_embd;
            const int fc_in = w.n_capture_layers * feat_per_cap;
            out.target_feat = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_BF16, fc_in, out.target_feat_cap);
            ggml_set_name(out.target_feat, "target_feat");
        } else {
            out.target_feat = nullptr;
        }

        out.base_buf = ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors(out.base_ctx, backend);
        if (!out.base_buf) {
            set_last_error("ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors failed for base cache");
            ggml_free(out.base_ctx);
            out.base_ctx = nullptr;
            return false;
        }
    }

    // ── Rollback context: snapshots + intermediates ───────────────────
    if (!prefill_only) {
        const int rb_tensors = 4 * n_delta;
        ggml_init_params ip{};
        ip.mem_size   = (size_t)(rb_tensors + 16) * ggml_tensor_overhead();
        ip.mem_buffer = nullptr;
        ip.no_alloc   = true;
        out.rollback_ctx = ggml_init(ip);
        if (!out.rollback_ctx) { set_last_error("rollback cache ggml_init failed"); return false; }

        int dn_idx = 0;
        for (int il = 0; il < w.n_layer; il++) {
            if (((il + 1) % w.full_attention_interval) != 0) {
                const bool owns_layer = il >= layer_begin && il < layer_end;
                if (!owns_layer) { dn_idx++; continue; }
                ggml_tensor * Sn = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                       head_v_dim, head_v_dim, w.ssm_dt_rank);
                ggml_tensor * Cn = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                       w.ssm_d_conv - 1, conv_ch);
                ggml_tensor * Si = ggml_new_tensor_4d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0,
                                                       head_v_dim, head_v_dim,
                                                       w.ssm_dt_rank, max_verify_tokens);
                ggml_tensor * Ci = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                       (w.ssm_d_conv - 1) + max_verify_tokens,
                                                       conv_ch, 1);
                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_state_snap_%d", il);  ggml_set_name(Sn, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_state_snap_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Cn, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_intermediate_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Si, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_input_cache_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Ci, name);
                out.ssm_state_snap[dn_idx]  = Sn;
                out.conv_state_snap[dn_idx] = Cn;
                out.ssm_intermediate[dn_idx] = Si;
                out.conv_input_cache[dn_idx] = Ci;
                dn_idx++;
            }
        }

        out.rollback_buf = ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors(out.rollback_ctx, backend);
        if (!out.rollback_buf) {
            set_last_error("ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors failed for rollback cache");
            ggml_free(out.rollback_ctx);
            out.rollback_ctx = nullptr;
            return false;
        }
    }

    // ── Zero-initialize all state tensors ─────────────────────────────
    std::vector<uint8_t> zeros(1 * 1024 * 1024, 0);
    ggml_context * ctx_list[] = { out.base_ctx, out.rollback_ctx };
    for (int ci = 0; ci < 2; ci++) {
        ggml_context * c = ctx_list[ci];
        if (!c) continue;
        for (ggml_tensor * t = ggml_get_first_tensor(c); t != nullptr;
             t = ggml_get_next_tensor(c, t)) {
            size_t nb = ggml_nbytes(t);
            size_t off = 0;
            while (off < nb) {
                size_t chunk = std::min(nb - off, zeros.size());
                ggml_backend_tensor_set(t, zeros.data(), off, chunk);
                off += chunk;
            }
        }
    }

    return true;
}

void free_target_cache(TargetCache & c) {
    if (c.base_buf)     { ggml_backend_buffer_free(c.base_buf);     c.base_buf     = nullptr; }
    if (c.base_ctx)     { ggml_free(c.base_ctx);                   c.base_ctx     = nullptr; }
    if (c.rollback_buf) { ggml_backend_buffer_free(c.rollback_buf); c.rollback_buf = nullptr; }
    if (c.rollback_ctx) { ggml_free(c.rollback_ctx);               c.rollback_ctx = nullptr; }
    c.attn_k.clear();
    c.attn_v.clear();
    c.ssm_state.clear();
    c.conv_state.clear();
    c.ssm_state_snap.clear();
    c.conv_state_snap.clear();
    c.ssm_intermediate.clear();
    c.conv_input_cache.clear();
    c.target_feat = nullptr;
    c.cur_pos = 0;
}

void reset_target_cache(TargetCache & c) {
    c.cur_pos = 0;
    std::vector<uint8_t> zeros(1 * 1024 * 1024, 0);
    ggml_context * ctx_list[] = { c.base_ctx, c.rollback_ctx };
    for (int ci = 0; ci < 2; ci++) {
        ggml_context * ctx = ctx_list[ci];
        if (!ctx) continue;
        for (ggml_tensor * t = ggml_get_first_tensor(ctx); t != nullptr;
             t = ggml_get_next_tensor(ctx, t)) {
            size_t nb = ggml_nbytes(t);
            size_t off = 0;
            while (off < nb) {
                size_t chunk = std::min(nb - off, zeros.size());
                ggml_backend_tensor_set(t, zeros.data(), off, chunk);
                off += chunk;
            }
        }
    }
}

void reset_recurrent_state(TargetCache & c) {
    auto zero_tensors = [](const std::vector<ggml_tensor *> & tensors) {
        std::vector<uint8_t> zeros;
        for (ggml_tensor * t : tensors) {
            if (!t) continue;
            const size_t nb = ggml_nbytes(t);
            if (zeros.size() < nb) zeros.resize(nb, 0);
            ggml_backend_tensor_set(t, zeros.data(), 0, nb);
        }
    };
    zero_tensors(c.ssm_state);
    zero_tensors(c.conv_state);
}

// Attach rollback tensors to an existing prefill cache without touching the
// base tensors (KV, SSM, conv, target_feat) that prefill already populated.
// No D2D copies — the base tensors stay right where the graph wrote them.
// If rollback tensors are already present (e.g. daemon mode second request),
// this is a no-op.
bool migrate_prefill_cache(const TargetWeights & w,
                           int max_ctx,
                           int max_verify_tokens,
                           ggml_backend_t backend,
                           TargetCache & cache) {
    // Already migrated (e.g. daemon mode second+ request after reset_target_cache).
    if (cache.rollback_ctx) return true;

    const int n_delta = (int)cache.ssm_state.size(); // 48
    const int head_v_dim = w.ssm_d_inner / w.ssm_dt_rank;
    const int conv_ch = w.ssm_d_inner + 2 * w.ssm_n_group * w.ssm_d_state;
    if (max_verify_tokens <= 0) {
        max_verify_tokens = DFLASH27B_DRAFT_BLOCK_SIZE;
    }

    cache.ssm_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    cache.conv_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    cache.ssm_intermediate.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    cache.conv_input_cache.assign(n_delta, nullptr);

    const int rb_tensors = 4 * n_delta;
    ggml_init_params ip{};
    ip.mem_size   = (size_t)(rb_tensors + 16) * ggml_tensor_overhead();
    ip.mem_buffer = nullptr;
    ip.no_alloc   = true;
    cache.rollback_ctx = ggml_init(ip);
    if (!cache.rollback_ctx) { set_last_error("rollback cache ggml_init failed"); return false; }

    int dn_idx = 0;
    for (int il = 0; il < w.n_layer; il++) {
        if (((il + 1) % w.full_attention_interval) != 0) {
            ggml_tensor * Sn = ggml_new_tensor_3d(cache.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                   head_v_dim, head_v_dim, w.ssm_dt_rank);
            ggml_tensor * Cn = ggml_new_tensor_2d(cache.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                   w.ssm_d_conv - 1, conv_ch);
            ggml_tensor * Si = ggml_new_tensor_4d(cache.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F16,
                                                   head_v_dim, head_v_dim,
                                                   w.ssm_dt_rank, max_verify_tokens);
            ggml_tensor * Ci = ggml_new_tensor_3d(cache.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                   (w.ssm_d_conv - 1) + max_verify_tokens,
                                                   conv_ch, 1);
            char name[64];
            std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_state_snap_%d", il);  ggml_set_name(Sn, name);
            std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_state_snap_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Cn, name);
            std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_intermediate_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Si, name);
            std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_input_cache_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Ci, name);
            cache.ssm_state_snap[dn_idx]  = Sn;
            cache.conv_state_snap[dn_idx] = Cn;
            cache.ssm_intermediate[dn_idx] = Si;
            cache.conv_input_cache[dn_idx] = Ci;
            dn_idx++;
        }
    }

    cache.rollback_buf = ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors(cache.rollback_ctx, backend);
    if (!cache.rollback_buf) {
        set_last_error("ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors failed for rollback cache");
        ggml_free(cache.rollback_ctx);
        cache.rollback_ctx = nullptr;
        return false;
    }

    // Zero-initialize rollback tensors
    std::vector<uint8_t> zeros(1 * 1024 * 1024, 0);
    for (ggml_tensor * t = ggml_get_first_tensor(cache.rollback_ctx); t != nullptr;
         t = ggml_get_next_tensor(cache.rollback_ctx, t)) {
        size_t nb = ggml_nbytes(t);
        size_t off = 0;
        while (off < nb) {
            size_t chunk = std::min(nb - off, zeros.size());
            ggml_backend_tensor_set(t, zeros.data(), off, chunk);
            off += chunk;
        }
    }

    return true;
}

// Snapshot/restore SSM+conv state for speculative rollback. Uses device-side
// tensor copy (ggml_backend_tensor_copy). Called outside of any compute graph.
void snapshot_ssm_state(TargetCache & c) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < c.ssm_state.size(); i++) {
        if (!c.ssm_state[i] || !c.ssm_state_snap[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.ssm_state[i], c.ssm_state_snap[i]);
        if (!c.conv_state[i] || !c.conv_state_snap[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.conv_state[i], c.conv_state_snap[i]);
    }
}

void restore_ssm_state(TargetCache & c) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < c.ssm_state.size(); i++) {
        if (!c.ssm_state_snap[i] || !c.ssm_state[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.ssm_state_snap[i], c.ssm_state[i]);
        if (!c.conv_state_snap[i] || !c.conv_state[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.conv_state_snap[i], c.conv_state[i]);
    }
}

// ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static ggml_tensor * build_swiglu_ffn(ggml_context * ctx, ggml_tensor * cur,
                                      const TargetLayer & L) {
    ggml_tensor * gate = apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_gate, cur), L.w_gate_s);   // [inter, n_tokens]
    gate = ggml_silu(ctx, gate);
    ggml_tensor * up = apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_up, cur), L.w_up_s);
    ggml_tensor * gu = ggml_mul(ctx, gate, up);
    return apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_down, gu), L.w_down_s);                  // [hidden, n_tokens]
}

1	# Plan — KVFlash 128K agentic on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B hybrid (ultracode session)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	In 2026, 128K agentic context is the baseline expectation. On a single RTX 3090, the
6	Qwen3.6-35B-A3B hybrid SSM-MoE today holds only ~90K context resident (Q3 experts ~13 GB +
7	core + the 10/40 attention layers' KV at ~81 KB/token; beyond ~90K the KV exceeds the ~7 GB
8	free). The just-shipped snapshot-restore fix (commit `53f63767`) collapses cross-turn prefill,
9	but it's mutually exclusive with paging, so >90K is currently a hard wall.
10	
11	KVFlash already solves exactly this on the **dense 27B** (RESULTS.md: pool 4K @ 64–256K → decode
12	flat ~38.6 tok/s = 1.4–2.9×, prefill 1.5–2.8×, KV VRAM 2304→18 MiB = 99% cut, needle 14–15/16;
13	drafter scorer 88–100% recall at 6–9% residency). It does NOT work on the qwen35moe hybrid because
14	**pooled chunked prefill** and **pooled snapshot save/restore** are unimplemented there
15	(qwen35-dense-only per DESIGN.md:141,270) — the MoE path hard-errors when prompt > pool.
16	
17	Goal: implement pooled prefill + pooled snapshot/restore + critical-chunk pinning for the
18	qwen35moe hybrid, gated on a definitive 128K quality bench, so the model serves 128K agentic
19	coding on a single 3090 at the dense-27B performance bar. **Drafter scorer gates the ship
20	decision** (it can page evicted chunks back; QK can't). Full stack, phased, each phase behind a
21	temp-0 bit-identity gate (silent-corruption class).
22	
23	## The enabling discovery (why this is tractable, not a rewrite)
24	
25	`Qwen35MoeBackend::hybrid_forward_batch()` (`server/src/qwen35moe/qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1578`)
26	is ALREADY a complete pooled + slot-masked + slot-mapped MoE forward — spec-decode verify/replay
27	call it every step. It does `alloc_span`+`slot_of` (1608), `kv_write_rows` (1614-1654), the
28	slot-space mask (1678-1708, identical recipe to dense `do_prefill` 1112-1138), in-place DeltaNet
29	state threading, and hot/cold/spark MoE FFN routing. **Pooled prefill = drive `hybrid_forward_batch`
30	in a chunk loop + delete two hard-errors.** Not a from-scratch port.
31	
32	Decode is already pool-paged (`run_pipelined_decode_path` slot_for per token + `kvflash_maybe_reselect`).
33	The one constraint: decode's cached attn path is MASKLESS (relies on zeroed free slots); the
34	prefill/batch path is MASKED. Pooled prefill uses the masked batch path; decode keeps the maskless
35	zeroed-slot contract. Both already exist — never touch the decode contract.
36	
37	## Dense reference (the template throughout)
38	
39	`Qwen35Backend::do_prefill()` `server/src/qwen35/qwen35_backend.cpp:954-1208`, the `kvf_paged`
40	branch (976-977): chunk loop, per-token `slot_for()` w/ live eviction, `kv_write_rows` matrix,
41	LOGICAL positions to `sg_.positions` (RoPE baked → relocation-safe), slot-space mask, post-prefill
42	`zero_free_blocks()` + mask-epoch bump. Pager core (architecture-agnostic, reuse as-is):
43	`server/src/common/kvflash_pager.h` — `slot_for` (165), `ensure_free_block` (322, sink+tail
44	protection then score_hook/LRU), `page_out/page_in`, `reselect` (286, τ-step).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Phase 1 — Pooled chunked prefill for qwen35moe (unblocks 128K prompts)
49	
50	- Delete the hard-error at `qwen35moe_backend.cpp:777-785` (generate) and `1401-1409` (restore).
51	- Add `kvf_paged = kvflash_active() && prompt_len > kvflash_tokens_ - chunk_tokens()` (mirror dense 976-977).
52	- When paged: `kvflash_pager_.reset()`, set chunk size = `chunk_tokens()` (align to pager blocks),
53	  loop calling `hybrid_forward_batch` once per `chunk_tokens`-chunk (per-chunk batch, NOT per-token —
54	  per-token is ~22× more dispatches). Eviction is automatic inside `hybrid_forward_batch`'s `alloc_span`.
55	- DeltaNet/conv state threads across chunks in-place automatically (orthogonal to KV paging).
56	- Post-prefill (paged branch): set `kvflash_history_`, `zero_free_blocks()`, bump mask epoch; do NOT
57	  call `kvflash_sync_prefill` (identity-only). Non-paged branch unchanged (no regression).
58	- Boundary snapshot guard fires only in the identity branch (Phase 2 lifts it).
59	
60	Gates: G1.1 temp-0 bit-identity sub-pool (identity path untouched); **G1.2 forced-paged vs identity,

The "temp-0 bit-identity" gate documented in the 2026-06-19 HANDOFF is not a harness script. It is a manual verification: run the server with `--temperature 0` on a substantive prompt (a 120-token tool-call), capture raw token IDs from restore path and cold-prefill path, compare char-for-char. I now have everything needed for a complete report. Here it is.

---

## 1. CURRENT `snapshot_save` Flow

`Qwen35MoeBackend` does NOT override `snapshot_save`. It inherits `Qwen35Backend::snapshot_save` verbatim.

**`Qwen35Backend::snapshot_save`** (qwen35_backend.cpp:406-426):

```cpp
bool Qwen35Backend::snapshot_save(int slot) {
    if (slot < 0 || slot >= PREFIX_SLOTS) return false;
    if (kvflash_active() &&
        (cache_.cur_pos > kvflash_tokens_ || !kvflash_pager_.is_identity())) {
        static bool warned = false;
        if (!warned) {
            std::fprintf(stderr, "[kvflash] snapshot skipped: cur_pos %d exceeds "
                                 "pool %d (pooled snapshots are a follow-up)\n",
                         cache_.cur_pos, kvflash_tokens_);
            warned = true;
        }
        return false;
    }
    PrefixSnapshot & snap = prefix_snapshots_[slot];
    return snapshot_target_cache(w_, cache_, snap_backend_, snap);
}
```

The guard at lines 413-423 is the exact insertion point for Phase-2: it returns false when `cur_pos > kvflash_tokens_` (pooled state exceeds resident pool) OR when the pager is no longer identity-mapped (eviction has happened). The comment says "pooled snapshots are a follow-up" — that follow-up is Phase-2.

`snapshot_target_cache` (qwen35_target_graph.cpp) allocates a `PrefixSnapshot` with: `attn_k_snap` (16 entries, n_full_attn), `attn_v_snap` (16), `ssm_state_snap` (48, n_delta), `conv_state_snap` (48), and `target_feat_snap`. Each is right-sized to `cache.cur_pos`, not `max_ctx`. Stored in the snap-backend (CPU on discrete GPU).

The **save trigger** in the MoE path is at qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1064-1088: after the pipelined hybrid prefill completes, if `req.snap_slot >= 0 && req.snap_pos > 0 && req.snap_pos == committed`, it calls `compute_logits()`, extracts the argmax into `target_cache().last_tok`, then calls `snapshot_save(req.snap_slot)`.

---

## 2. CURRENT Restore Path (on `feat/kvflash-moe-128k`, i.e. after 8156896f)

**`Qwen35MoeBackend::restore_and_generate_impl`** (qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1369-1493):

Entry guard: if `!target_weights().moe_hybrid`, delegates to `Qwen35Backend::restore_and_generate_impl` (the dense path). Otherwise the MoE-specific path:

1. **Validate** slot is used; set sampler config.
2. **Temp-sampling fallback** (line 1390-1394): if `n_gen > 0 && temp > 0`, falls back to full `generate_impl`. (This is the 8156896f behavior; 53f63767 removes this and makes temp work via the delta path.)
3. **Graph reset** (lines 1396-1400): `pipe_state_.reset()` + free hot/cold graphs for all MoE layers.
4. **`restore_target_cache_from_snapshot(slot)`** (line 1402): calls `restore_target_cache(prefix_snapshots_[slot], cache_)` which does device-to-device copies of all KV rows + SSM states + conv states + target_feat back into `cache_`. Sets `cache_.cur_pos = snap.cur_pos`.
5. **kvflash identity re-map** (lines 1435-1443): `kvflash_pager_.reset()`, then `kvflash_pager_.alloc_span(0, snap_pos)` to map `[0, snap_pos)` identity-style in the pager, then `zero_free_blocks()`.
6. **Residual delta-prefill** (lines 1447-1462): token-by-token `hybrid_forward_one_token(req.prompt[i], committed, act_cur, argmax)` for `i` in `[snap_pos, prompt_len)`. Each call runs the full 40-layer pipelined decode forward (SSM + attention + hot/cold MoE FFN), advancing `committed` and `target_cache().cur_pos`.
7. **`kvflash_sync_prefill`** (lines 1464-1473): rebuilds the pager eviction policy over `[0, committed)`. If `prompt_len == committed` uses real token IDs; otherwise uses `kv_offset=committed` for restore-only path (unknown-prefix history).
8. **Decode dispatch** (lines 1475-1488): if `last_tok < 0`, falls back to `generate_impl`. Otherwise calls `run_pipelined_decode_path(committed, n_gen, ...)`.

**What `restore_target_cache` does NOT do**: it does NOT replay SSM intermediates or `conv_input_cache`. The comment at internal.h:439-441 says: "Does NOT touch ssm_intermediate / conv_input_cache — those will be repopulated by the first decode step's verify forward." This is safe because the snapshot carries the SSM recurrent _state_ (the accumulated matrix state), not the per-step intermediates.

---

## 3. Commit 53f63767 vs Current HEAD — Verdict

**8156896f IS an ancestor of current HEAD** (feat/kvflash-moe-128k). **53f63767 is NOT on current branch** — it lives only on `feat/pflash-qwen35moe-280`.

The current HEAD's `restore_and_generate_impl` is the 8156896f version. The 53f63767 diff on top of 8156896f adds three substantive things that are absent from HEAD:

**A. Early no-delta fallback** (53f63767 lines 1360-1382 in its tree): If `prompt_len <= snap_pos`, immediately returns `generate_impl`. Currently on HEAD (line 1390-1394) only `temp > 0` falls back; an exact-hit (no-delta) turn incorrectly tries to decode with `last_tok = -1` which then triggers the separate `generate_impl` fallback at line 1476-1479 — same outcome but messier.

**B. Feature-mirror re-sync after restore** (53f63767 adds ~11 lines after the delta loop): `draft_feature_mirror_sync_range(target_cache().target_feat, target_cache().target_feat_cap, feature_mirror(), start, n)`. Currently HEAD does NOT do this re-sync. This means post-restore spec-decode starts with a stale feature ring — the draft will use wrong features from the previous session. This is a correctness gap.

**C. Spec-decode dispatch in the restore path** (53f63767 adds `can_hybrid_spec` check + `do_hybrid_spec_decode` call): Currently HEAD calls only `run_pipelined_decode_path` (AR). 53f63767 dispatches to `do_hybrid_spec_decode` when all conditions are met (temp==0, draft, not parked, etc.). HEAD always runs AR after a restore.

**Cherry-pick test**: `git cherry-pick --no-commit 53f63767` completed with **auto-merge, zero conflicts** on the current branch. The Phase-1 pooled-prefill edit touches `generate_impl` (the `kvf_paged` block, ~lines 771-1060 in HEAD), while 53f63767 modifies `run_pipelined_decode_path` (GPU argmax, `project_logits` signature) and `restore_and_generate_impl`. These are non-overlapping hunks.

**RECOMMENDATION**: Cherry-pick 53f63767 as-is. It applies cleanly. The three additions (no-delta early exit, feature-mirror re-sync, spec-decode dispatch in restore) are all needed for Phase-2 correctness — especially B (feature-mirror re-sync) and C (spec-decode in restore). Do NOT hand-integrate separately; the auto-merge result is correct. After cherry-picking, Phase-2 can layer the pooled-blob save on top cleanly.

---

## 4. Disk-Cache Snapshot Slot Path

The disk cache serializes snapshots via `DiskPrefixCache::write_file` (disk_prefix_cache.cpp:625-684).

**Format**: `<cache_dir>/<layout_fingerprint_hex>/<token_hash_hex>.dkv` — 80-byte `DiskCacheHeader` (magic "DKVC", version, layout_id SHA-1, cur_pos, n_tensors, token_hash, payload_bytes, last_tok) + tensor name/type/shape table + raw tensor data (4 MB chunked via `ggml_backend_tensor_get`).

**The key seam is `ModelBackend::SnapshotRef`** (model_backend.h:249-253):
```cpp
struct SnapshotRef {
    ggml_context        * ctx     = nullptr;
    ggml_backend_buffer_t buf     = nullptr;
    int                   cur_pos = 0;
    int32_t               last_tok = -1;
};
```
`write_file` iterates `ggml_get_first_tensor(ref.ctx)` and writes every tensor in the context. The `kvflash_blob` for Phase-2 would need to either: (a) be included as named tensors in the PrefixSnapshot's ggml_context so it rides the existing `write_file` path unchanged, or (b) be a separate sidecar field in `SnapshotRef` with a separate write path.

**The clean approach for Phase-2**: store the kvflash blob as additional named tensors (`kvflash_pgtable` or similar) in the PrefixSnapshot's existing `ctx`/`buf`. Then `write_file` serializes them for free with zero changes to disk_prefix_cache.cpp. On `read_file`/`snapshot_adopt`, `Qwen35Backend::snapshot_adopt` (qwen35_backend.cpp:460+) already walks tensors by name via `sscanf` — adding another `sscanf` pattern for `kvflash_*` tensors is the natural extension point.

**`snapshot_adopt`** is the load side: `read_file` (disk_prefix_cache.cpp:688-785) reconstructs the ggml_context + CPU buffer then calls `backend_.snapshot_adopt(slot, ctx, buf, cur_pos, last_tok)`. Currently `snapshot_adopt` only rebinds `snap_cache_k_N`, `snap_cache_v_N`, `snap_ssm_state_N`, `snap_conv_state_N`, `snap_target_feat`. A `kvflash_pgtable` tensor would need one more `else if` branch here.

---

## 5. PrefixSnapshot Consumers

All sites that construct, read, or hold a `PrefixSnapshot`:

**Struct definition**: `server/src/internal.h:398-426`

**Functions on PrefixSnapshot** (all in qwen35_target_graph.cpp):
- `snapshot_target_cache(w, cache, backend, snap)` — thick save
- `restore_target_cache(snap, cache)` — thick restore

All servers killed. VRAM back to 1023/24576 MiB baseline. Now I have the complete picture. Let me write the definitive report.

---

**STEP 0: RESTORE TRIGGER ANALYSIS**

The snapshot save is triggered at `qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1096`:
```cpp
if (req.snap_slot >= 0 && req.snap_pos > 0 && req.snap_pos == committed)
```
where `committed = prompt_len` (full prompt length after prefill). `snap_slot/snap_pos` come from `prefix_cache_.prepare_inline_snap()` (http_server.cpp:2625), which sets `snap_pos` to the second-to-last `<|im_end|>` boundary in the prompt — a position *inside* the prompt, not at its end.

The condition `snap_pos == committed` is **never true** in the standard single-request flow because `snap_pos` (chat boundary, e.g. 983) always differs from `committed` (full prompt length, e.g. 1018). The snapshot save fires only if the server were to prefill exactly `snap_pos` tokens — which would require a two-phase request or a custom prefill-to-boundary API that doesn't exist.

The in-VRAM path (req2 restoring from `prefix_snapshots_[slot].kvflash_blob`) is correct in principle: the blob is a `std::vector<uint8_t>` held in host memory within the in-process struct, not on disk. There is no disk read on req2. But this path is never reached because the snapshot is never written.

**Flags used:** `--kvflash N` and `DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB=4000`. No disk cache flags needed or used — the restore path is entirely in-VRAM.

---

**(1) RESTORE TRIGGER**

The only flag activating kvflash pooled snapshot/restore is `--kvflash N`. `DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB=4000` is required to activate the MoE hybrid path. There is no `--disk-prefix-cache` or `--kv-cache-dir` involved — the kvflash blob lives in `prefix_snapshots_[slot].kvflash_blob` (a `std::vector<uint8_t>` in host RAM, in-process). Req2 in the same process would use this in-RAM slot directly — no disk read.

However: **the snapshot save condition (`req.snap_pos == committed`) is never satisfied**, so `snapshot_used(snap_slot)` always returns false, `abort_inline_snap` is called, the prefix cache entry is never created, and req2 always gets `restore=false`.

**(2) G2.1 VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE (restore path not exercised)**

- Diff between REF and WARM req2: **empty — outputs identical**
- But `restore=false` on all 3 requests. The outputs match because both arms independently ran full prefill on the same deterministic prompt (temp=0). The snapshot/restore code path was never executed.
- Root cause: "hybrid skip unsafe boundary" — `snap_pos=983 != committed=1018` for all 3 requests.
- No crash, no assert, no error. Server ran cleanly.

**(3) G2.2 VERDICT: NEEDS STEP 2B — restore trigger not firing**

- Diff between REF and WARM req2: **empty — outputs identical** (same reason as G2.1)
- Pooled prefill DID fire as expected: `[kvflash] hybrid pooled prefill: 1018 tokens (64-token chunks, evicting)` (pool=1024, prompt=1018 > 960 threshold).
- But snapshot still not saved: `[snap] hybrid skip unsafe boundary slot=N req_snap_pos=983 cur_pos=1018` on all 3 requests.
- `is_pooled` was never set to `true`. `kvflash_blob` never populated. `restore_and_generate` never called.
- No crash, no assert.

**Evidence quoted from logs:**

G2.1 (kvflash=4096, non-pooled path):
```
[server] chat CACHE chatcmpl_0000000000000000 restore=false slot=-1 prefix_len=0 effective_prompt=1018 pflash=false disk_policy=full disk_hit=false snap_slot=0 snap_pos=983
[snap] hybrid skip unsafe boundary slot=0 req_snap_pos=983 cur_pos=1018
```

G2.2 (kvflash=1024, pooled path active):
```
[server] chat CACHE chatcmpl_0000000000000000 restore=false slot=-1 prefix_len=0 effective_prompt=1018 pflash=false disk_policy=full disk_hit=false snap_slot=0 snap_pos=983
[kvflash] hybrid pooled prefill: 1018 tokens (64-token chunks, evicting)
[snap] hybrid skip unsafe boundary slot=0 req_snap_pos=983 cur_pos=1018
```

**(4) First divergence point**: N/A — no divergence in outputs (both PASS on output text), but the restore logic was never reached.

**(5) Crash/assert**: None.

---

**ROOT CAUSE — what needs fixing for real G2 gates:**

The snapshot save guard in `qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1096` requires `req.snap_pos == committed` (i.e., the prefix boundary must equal the full prompt length). This is never true in normal operation because `prepare_inline_snap` returns a boundary *inside* the prompt (second-to-last `<|im_end|>`), while `generate()` always processes the full prompt.

The dense backend (`qwen35_backend.cpp`) has the same guard at the corresponding location and faces the same issue. The MoE Phase-2 pooled snapshot code is correct (save sets `is_pooled=true` + serializes `kvflash_blob`; restore at line 1462 deserializes it), but it is structurally unreachable via the standard single-pass `generate()` API.

1. Change the snap condition from `req.snap_pos == committed` to `req.snap_pos <= committed` and save at the boundary mid-prefill (requires stopping the prefill loop at `snap_pos`, computing logits, saving, then continuing — analogous to the disk cold-prefix path at http_server.cpp:2596-2619).
2. Add a direct test API that calls `generate()` with `snap_slot` and a prompt exactly equal to `snap_pos` tokens (the "prefix-only" sub-request), then calls `restore_and_generate` for the full prompt — mirroring what the disk cold-prefix path does.

            {"tokenizer_id", config.tokenizer_id.empty() ? json(nullptr) : json(config.tokenizer_id)},
        }},

            {"backend",         config.runtime_backend.empty() ? "cuda" : config.runtime_backend},
            {"fa_window",       config.fa_window},

            {"chunk",           config.chunk},

        // See spec §4.2.
        {"budget_envelope", {

                                ? json(config.ddtree_budget) : json(nullptr)},
        }},
        {"sampling", {
            {"capabilities", {
                {"supports_temperature",        true},
                {"supports_top_p",              true},
                {"supports_top_k",              true},
                {"supports_frequency_penalty",  true},
                {"supports_seed",               true},
            }},
        }},
        {"pflash", pflash},
        {"prefix_cache", {
            {"capacity",      pcs.capacity},
            {"in_use",        pcs.in_use},
            {"lifetime_hits", pcs.lifetime_hits},
        }},
        {"full_cache", {
            {"enabled",       pcfs.enabled},
            {"capacity",      pcfs.capacity},
            {"in_use",        pcfs.in_use},
            {"disk_bytes",    pcfs.disk_bytes},
            {"lifetime_hits", pcfs.lifetime_hits},
        }},
        {"tool_replay", {
            {"max_entries",     tms.max_entries},
            {"max_bytes",       tms.max_bytes},
            {"current_entries", tms.current_entries},
            {"current_bytes",   tms.current_bytes},
        }},
        // The C++ daemon is linked in-process; if /props is responding,
        // the daemon is alive by construction.
        {"daemon", {{"alive", true}}},
        {"api", {{"endpoints", kApiEndpoints}}},
        // Capability flags surfaced for clients that don't want to crack
        // open `reasoning` / `speculative` / etc. — matches the Python
        // server's _capabilities() helper.
        {"capabilities", {
            {"reasoning_supported",   reasoning_supported},
            {"speculative_supported", speculative_supported},
            {"tools_supported",       tools_supported},
        }},
    };
    return body;
}

// Normalize Anthropic's `system` field (top-level on /v1/messages and
// /v1/messages/count_tokens) into a leading `{role:"system", content:...}`
// entry on `messages`. Accepts either a flat string or an array of typed
// blocks (`[{type:"text", text:"..."}]`), and strips any
// `x-anthropic-billing-header:`-prefixed block injected by Claude Code so
// it never reaches the model or the token counter.
//
// Side-effect: prepends a system message to `messages` when the body has
// a non-empty `system` field after billing-header filtering. No-op
// otherwise. Both endpoints call this with identical semantics — having
// one helper guarantees token counting and generation can't drift.
static void normalize_anthropic_system(const json & body, json & messages) {
    if (!body.contains("system")) return;
    json sys_content = body["system"];
    if (sys_content.is_array()) {
        json filtered = json::array();
        for (const auto & block : sys_content) {
            if (block.is_object() && block.value("type", "") == "text") {
                std::string text = block.value("text", "");
                if (text.rfind("x-anthropic-billing-header:", 0) == 0) {
                    continue;  // skip Claude Code billing header block
                }
            }
            filtered.push_back(block);
        }
        sys_content = std::move(filtered);
    } else if (sys_content.is_string()) {
        std::string s = sys_content.get<std::string>();
        if (s.rfind("x-anthropic-billing-header:", 0) == 0) {
            sys_content = "";
        }
    }
    if (!sys_content.empty()) {
        json sys_msg = {{"role", "system"}, {"content", sys_content}};
        messages.insert(messages.begin(), sys_msg);
    }
}

json parse_responses_arguments(const json & item) {
    if (!item.contains("arguments")) return json::object();
    const auto & arguments = item["arguments"];
    if (arguments.is_object()) return arguments;
    if (arguments.is_string()) {
        try {
            return json::parse(arguments.get<std::string>());
        } catch (const std::exception &) {
            return json::object();
        }
    }
    return json::object();
}

std::string render_tool_call_xml(const std::string & name, const json & arguments) {
    std::string out = "<function=" + name + ">\n";
    if (arguments.is_object()) {
        for (const auto & [key, value] : arguments.items()) {
            out += "<parameter=" + key + ">\n";
            out += value.is_string() ? value.get<std::string>() : value.dump();
            out += "\n</parameter>\n";
        }
    }
    out += "</function>\n";
    return out;
}

std::vector<ChatMessage> normalize_chat_messages(
    const json & messages,
    ApiFormat format,
    ToolMemory & tool_memory) {
    std::vector<ChatMessage> chat_msgs;
    std::vector<std::string> system_parts;

    if (messages.is_array()) {
        for (const auto & m : messages) {
            if (format == ApiFormat::RESPONSES && m.is_object()) {
                std::string item_type = m.value("type", "message");
                if (item_type == "function_call") {
                    std::string call_id = m.value("call_id", m.value("id", ""));
                    std::string raw;
                    if (!call_id.empty()) {
                        raw = tool_memory.lookup({call_id});
                    }
                    if (raw.empty()) {
                        raw = render_tool_call_xml(m.value("name", ""),
                                                   parse_responses_arguments(m));
                    }
                    chat_msgs.push_back({"assistant", raw});
                    continue;
                }
                if (item_type == "function_call_output") {
                    std::string output;
                    if (m.contains("output") && m["output"].is_string()) {
                        output = m["output"].get<std::string>();
                    } else if (m.contains("output")) {
                        output = m["output"].dump();
                    }
                    chat_msgs.push_back({"tool", output,
                                         m.value("call_id", m.value("id", ""))});
                    continue;
                }
            }

            ChatMessage cm;
            cm.role = m.value("role", "user");

            bool replayed = false;
            if (cm.role == "assistant" && m.contains("tool_calls") &&
                m["tool_calls"].is_array() && !m["tool_calls"].empty()) {
                std::vector<std::string> call_ids;
                for (const auto & tc : m["tool_calls"]) {
                    std::string id = tc.value("id", "");
                    if (!id.empty()) call_ids.push_back(id);
                }
                std::string raw = tool_memory.lookup(call_ids);
                if (!raw.empty()) {
                    cm.content = raw;
                    replayed = true;
                }
            }

            if (!replayed) {
                if (m.contains("content") && m["content"].is_string()) {
                    cm.content = m["content"].get<std::string>();
                } else if (m.contains("content") && m["content"].is_array()) {
                    for (const auto & part : m["content"]) {
                        std::string ptype = part.value("type", "");
                        if (ptype == "text" || ptype == "input_text" ||
                            ptype == "output_text") {
                            cm.content += part.value("text", "");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            if (format == ApiFormat::RESPONSES &&
                (cm.role == "system" || cm.role == "developer")) {
                system_parts.push_back(cm.content);
            } else {
                chat_msgs.push_back(std::move(cm));
            }
        }
    } else if (messages.is_string()) {
        chat_msgs.push_back({"user", messages.get<std::string>()});
    }

    if (!system_parts.empty()) {
        std::string merged_system;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < system_parts.size(); i++) {
            if (i) merged_system += "\n\n";
            merged_system += system_parts[i];
        }
        chat_msgs.insert(chat_msgs.begin(), {"system", merged_system});
    }

    return chat_msgs;
}
