bool create_target_cache(const TargetWeights & w,
                         int max_ctx,
                         int max_verify_tokens,
                         ggml_backend_t backend,
                         TargetCache & out,
                         bool prefill_only) {
    return create_target_cache_partial(w, max_ctx, max_verify_tokens, backend,
                                       out, prefill_only,
                                       0, w.n_layer, true);
}

bool create_target_cache_partial(const TargetWeights & w,
                                 int max_ctx,
                                 int max_verify_tokens,
                                 ggml_backend_t backend,
                                 TargetCache & out,
                                 bool prefill_only,
                                 int layer_begin,
                                 int layer_end,
                                 bool allocate_target_feat) {
    if (layer_begin < 0) layer_begin = 0;
    if (layer_end < 0 || layer_end > w.n_layer) layer_end = w.n_layer;
    if (layer_begin > layer_end) {
        set_last_error("invalid target cache layer range");
        return false;
    }
    out.backend = backend;
    out.max_ctx = max_ctx;
    out.cur_pos = 0;

    const int n_full_attn = w.n_layer / w.full_attention_interval; // 16
    const int n_delta     = w.n_layer - n_full_attn;               // 48

    const int head_v_dim  = w.ssm_d_inner / w.ssm_dt_rank;
    const int conv_ch     = w.ssm_d_inner + 2 * w.ssm_n_group * w.ssm_d_state;

    out.attn_k.assign(n_full_attn, nullptr);
    out.attn_v.assign(n_full_attn, nullptr);
    out.ssm_state.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_state.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.ssm_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_state_snap.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.ssm_intermediate.assign(n_delta, nullptr);
    out.conv_input_cache.assign(n_delta, nullptr);

    // KV cache element types (resolved from env; aborts on unsupported pair).
    ggml_type kv_k_type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0;
    ggml_type kv_v_type = GGML_TYPE_Q8_0;
    dflash::resolve_kv_types(kv_k_type, kv_v_type);
    out.kv_k_type = kv_k_type;
    out.kv_v_type = kv_v_type;

    // Graph-level FWHT K-rotation (TurboQuant-style outlier spreading with
    // standard quant types that keep fast FA kernel paths on all arches).
    // Skip for TQ3_0 K cache — that type already applies WHT during quantization.
    out.kv_k_rotated = (kv_k_type != GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0);

    const bool needs_256_stride =
        kv_k_type == GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0 || kv_v_type == GGML_TYPE_TQ3_0;
    const int max_ctx_alloc = needs_256_stride
        ? ((max_ctx + 255) / 256) * 256
        : max_ctx;

    // ── Base context: KV cache + SSM/conv state + target_feat ────────
    {
        const int base_tensors = 2 * n_full_attn + 2 * n_delta + 1;
        ggml_init_params ip{};
        ip.mem_size   = (size_t)(base_tensors + 16) * ggml_tensor_overhead();
        ip.mem_buffer = nullptr;
        ip.no_alloc   = true;
        out.base_ctx = ggml_init(ip);
        if (!out.base_ctx) { set_last_error("base cache ggml_init failed"); return false; }

        int fa_idx = 0, dn_idx = 0;
        for (int il = 0; il < w.n_layer; il++) {
            const bool is_attn = (((il + 1) % w.full_attention_interval) == 0);
            const bool owns_layer = il >= layer_begin && il < layer_end;
            if (is_attn) {
                if (!owns_layer) { fa_idx++; continue; }
                // [head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, n_head_kv]
                ggml_tensor * K = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, kv_k_type,
                                                     head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, w.n_head_kv);
                ggml_tensor * V = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, kv_v_type,
                                                     head_dim, max_ctx_alloc, w.n_head_kv);
                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "cache_k_%d", il);
                ggml_set_name(K, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "cache_v_%d", il);
                ggml_set_name(V, name);
                out.attn_k[fa_idx] = K;
                out.attn_v[fa_idx] = V;

            } else {
                if (!owns_layer) { dn_idx++; continue; }
                // ssm_state: [head_v_dim, head_v_dim, num_v_heads]
                ggml_tensor * S = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,

                ggml_tensor * C = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,

                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_state_%d", il);  ggml_set_name(S, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_state_%d", il); ggml_set_name(C, name);
                out.ssm_state[dn_idx]  = S;
                out.conv_state[dn_idx] = C;
                dn_idx++;
            }
        }

        constexpr int TARGET_FEAT_CAP_DEFAULT = 4096;
        out.target_feat_cap = std::min(max_ctx, TARGET_FEAT_CAP_DEFAULT);
        if (allocate_target_feat) {
            const int feat_per_cap = (out.feat_dim_per_capture > 0)
                ? out.feat_dim_per_capture : (int)w.n_embd;
            const int fc_in = w.n_capture_layers * feat_per_cap;
            out.target_feat = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.base_ctx, GGML_TYPE_BF16, fc_in, out.target_feat_cap);

            out.target_feat = nullptr;

        out.base_buf = ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors(out.base_ctx, backend);
        if (!out.base_buf) {

            return false;

    if (!prefill_only) {
        const int rb_tensors = 4 * n_delta;
        ggml_init_params ip{};
        ip.mem_size   = (size_t)(rb_tensors + 16) * ggml_tensor_overhead();
        ip.mem_buffer = nullptr;
        ip.no_alloc   = true;
        out.rollback_ctx = ggml_init(ip);
        if (!out.rollback_ctx) { set_last_error("rollback cache ggml_init failed"); return false; }

        int dn_idx = 0;
        for (int il = 0; il < w.n_layer; il++) {
            if (((il + 1) % w.full_attention_interval) != 0) {
                const bool owns_layer = il >= layer_begin && il < layer_end;
                if (!owns_layer) { dn_idx++; continue; }
                ggml_tensor * Sn = ggml_new_tensor_3d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,

                ggml_tensor * Cn = ggml_new_tensor_2d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_F32,
                                                       w.ssm_d_conv - 1, conv_ch);
                ggml_tensor * Si = ggml_new_tensor_4d(out.rollback_ctx, GGML_TYPE_Q8_0,

                char name[64];
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_state_snap_%d", il);  ggml_set_name(Sn, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_state_snap_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Cn, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "ssm_intermediate_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Si, name);
                std::snprintf(name, sizeof(name), "conv_input_cache_%d", il); ggml_set_name(Ci, name);
                out.ssm_state_snap[dn_idx]  = Sn;
                out.conv_state_snap[dn_idx] = Cn;

        out.rollback_buf = ggml_backend_alloc_ctx_tensors(out.rollback_ctx, backend);
        if (!out.rollback_buf) {

    std::vector<uint8_t> zeros(1 * 1024 * 1024, 0);
    ggml_context * ctx_list[] = { out.base_ctx, out.rollback_ctx };
    for (int ci = 0; ci < 2; ci++) {
        ggml_context * c = ctx_list[ci];

    if (c.base_ctx)     { ggml_free(c.base_ctx);                   c.base_ctx     = nullptr; }
    if (c.rollback_buf) { ggml_backend_buffer_free(c.rollback_buf); c.rollback_buf = nullptr; }
    if (c.rollback_ctx) { ggml_free(c.rollback_ctx);               c.rollback_ctx = nullptr; }

void reset_recurrent_state(TargetCache & c) {
    auto zero_tensors = [](const std::vector<ggml_tensor *> & tensors) {
        std::vector<uint8_t> zeros;
        for (ggml_tensor * t : tensors) {
            if (!t) continue;
            const size_t nb = ggml_nbytes(t);

    return true;
}

// Snapshot/restore SSM+conv state for speculative rollback. Uses device-side
// tensor copy (ggml_backend_tensor_copy). Called outside of any compute graph.
void snapshot_ssm_state(TargetCache & c) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < c.ssm_state.size(); i++) {
        if (!c.ssm_state[i] || !c.ssm_state_snap[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.ssm_state[i], c.ssm_state_snap[i]);
        if (!c.conv_state[i] || !c.conv_state_snap[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.conv_state[i], c.conv_state_snap[i]);
    }
}

void restore_ssm_state(TargetCache & c) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < c.ssm_state.size(); i++) {
        if (!c.ssm_state_snap[i] || !c.ssm_state[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.ssm_state_snap[i], c.ssm_state[i]);
        if (!c.conv_state_snap[i] || !c.conv_state[i]) continue;
        ggml_backend_tensor_copy(c.conv_state_snap[i], c.conv_state[i]);
    }
}

// ─── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

static ggml_tensor * build_swiglu_ffn(ggml_context * ctx, ggml_tensor * cur,
                                      const TargetLayer & L) {
    ggml_tensor * gate = apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_gate, cur), L.w_gate_s);   // [inter, n_tokens]
    gate = ggml_silu(ctx, gate);
    ggml_tensor * up = apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_up, cur), L.w_up_s);
    ggml_tensor * gu = ggml_mul(ctx, gate, up);
    return apply_scale2(ctx, ggml_mul_mat(ctx, L.w_down, gu), L.w_down_s);                  // [hidden, n_tokens]
}

1	# Plan — KVFlash 128K agentic on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B hybrid (ultracode session)
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	In 2026, 128K agentic context is the baseline expectation. On a single RTX 3090, the
6	Qwen3.6-35B-A3B hybrid SSM-MoE today holds only ~90K context resident (Q3 experts ~13 GB +
7	core + the 10/40 attention layers' KV at ~81 KB/token; beyond ~90K the KV exceeds the ~7 GB
8	free). The just-shipped snapshot-restore fix (commit `53f63767`) collapses cross-turn prefill,
9	but it's mutually exclusive with paging, so >90K is currently a hard wall.
10	
11	KVFlash already solves exactly this on the **dense 27B** (RESULTS.md: pool 4K @ 64–256K → decode
12	flat ~38.6 tok/s = 1.4–2.9×, prefill 1.5–2.8×, KV VRAM 2304→18 MiB = 99% cut, needle 14–15/16;
13	drafter scorer 88–100% recall at 6–9% residency). It does NOT work on the qwen35moe hybrid because
14	**pooled chunked prefill** and **pooled snapshot save/restore** are unimplemented there
15	(qwen35-dense-only per DESIGN.md:141,270) — the MoE path hard-errors when prompt > pool.
16	
17	Goal: implement pooled prefill + pooled snapshot/restore + critical-chunk pinning for the
18	qwen35moe hybrid, gated on a definitive 128K quality bench, so the model serves 128K agentic
19	coding on a single 3090 at the dense-27B performance bar. **Drafter scorer gates the ship
20	decision** (it can page evicted chunks back; QK can't). Full stack, phased, each phase behind a
21	temp-0 bit-identity gate (silent-corruption class).
22	
23	## The enabling discovery (why this is tractable, not a rewrite)
24	
25	`Qwen35MoeBackend::hybrid_forward_batch()` (`server/src/qwen35moe/qwen35moe_backend.cpp:1578`)
26	is ALREADY a complete pooled + slot-masked + slot-mapped MoE forward — spec-decode verify/replay
27	call it every step. It does `alloc_span`+`slot_of` (1608), `kv_write_rows` (1614-1654), the
28	slot-space mask (1678-1708, identical recipe to dense `do_prefill` 1112-1138), in-place DeltaNet
29	state threading, and hot/cold/spark MoE FFN routing. **Pooled prefill = drive `hybrid_forward_batch`
30	in a chunk loop + delete two hard-errors.** Not a from-scratch port.
31	
32	Decode is already pool-paged (`run_pipelined_decode_path` slot_for per token + `kvflash_maybe_reselect`).
33	The one constraint: decode's cached attn path is MASKLESS (relies on zeroed free slots); the
34	prefill/batch path is MASKED. Pooled prefill uses the masked batch path; decode keeps the maskless
35	zeroed-slot contract. Both already exist — never touch the decode contract.
36	
37	## Dense reference (the template throughout)
38	
39	`Qwen35Backend::do_prefill()` `server/src/qwen35/qwen35_backend.cpp:954-1208`, the `kvf_paged`
40	branch (976-977): chunk loop, per-token `slot_for()` w/ live eviction, `kv_write_rows` matrix,
41	LOGICAL positions to `sg_.positions` (RoPE baked → relocation-safe), slot-space mask, post-prefill
42	`zero_free_blocks()` + mask-epoch bump. Pager core (architecture-agnostic, reuse as-is):
43	`server/src/common/kvflash_pager.h` — `slot_for` (165), `ensure_free_block` (322, sink+tail
44	protection then score_hook/LRU), `page_out/page_in`, `reselect` (286, τ-step).
45	
46	---
47	
48	## Phase 1 — Pooled chunked prefill for qwen35moe (unblocks 128K prompts)
49	
50	- Delete the hard-error at `qwen35moe_backend.cpp:777-785` (generate) and `1401-1409` (restore).
51	- Add `kvf_paged = kvflash_active() && prompt_len > kvflash_tokens_ - chunk_tokens()` (mirror dense 976-977).
52	- When paged: `kvflash_pager_.reset()`, set chunk size = `chunk_tokens()` (align to pager blocks),
53	  loop calling `hybrid_forward_batch` once per `chunk_tokens`-chunk (per-chunk batch, NOT per-token —
54	  per-token is ~22× more dispatches). Eviction is automatic inside `hybrid_forward_batch`'s `alloc_span`.
55	- DeltaNet/conv state threads across chunks in-place automatically (orthogonal to KV paging).
56	- Post-prefill (paged branch): set `kvflash_history_`, `zero_free_blocks()`, bump mask epoch; do NOT
57	  call `kvflash_sync_prefill` (identity-only). Non-paged branch unchanged (no regression).
58	- Boundary snapshot guard fires only in the identity branch (Phase 2 lifts it).
59	
60	Gates: G1.1 temp-0 bit-identity sub-pool (identity path untouched); **G1.2 forced-paged vs identity,
61	bit-identical with cold experts present** (isolates set_rows+mask+MoE-routing from eviction);
62	G1.3 128K prompt prefills with flat VRAM, coherent decode; G1.4 eviction correctness (evicted-middle
63	needle gone, sink/tail needle retained, `page_outs>0`).
64	
65	## Phase 2 — Pooled snapshot save/restore (composes with the restore-collapse)
66	
67	- NEW `serialize()`/`deserialize()` in `kvflash_pager.h` (NOT present today — file ends ~385).
68	  `serialize` emits KV bytes in LOGICAL chunk order (gather resident via `copy_chunk` segment walk,
69	  copy `host_data` for paged); `deserialize` rebuilds a fresh page table via `slot_for` (evicting as
70	  pool fills, stashing overflow to `host_data`). Factor a `for_each_segment(chunk,block,fn)` helper.
71	- Extend `PrefixSnapshot` (`server/src/qwen35/internal.h`): `kvflash_blob` + `is_pooled`. Add `skip_kv`
72	  flag to `snapshot_target_cache`/`restore_target_cache` (qwen35_target_graph.cpp:1385-1599) — SSM/conv/
73	  target_feat keep the existing fixed-size tensor path; KV goes through the blob when pooled.
74	- Override `snapshot_save` in `Qwen35MoeBackend`: replace the `return false` pooled guard
75	  (qwen35_backend.cpp:413-423) with the pooled serialize path. Pooled `restore_and_generate_impl`:
76	  `deserialize` instead of `alloc_span(0,snap_pos)`; route residual delta-prefill through the Phase 1
77	  chunked path; guard `kvflash_sync_prefill` behind `!is_pooled`. Store the 128K blob to the disk-cache
78	  slot path, not VRAM.
79	
80	Gates: G2.1 in-pool round-trip bit-identical; **G2.2 round-trip AFTER eviction (`!is_identity`)
81	bit-identical**; G2.3 cross-turn 128K save→restore→delta, flat VRAM; G2.4 identity-path no-regression.
82	
83	## Phase 3 — Critical-chunk pinning + drafter scorer + composition
84	
85	- Drafter scorer (`server/src/qwen3/qwen3_kvflash_scorer.h`) as the residency policy — already loaded
86	  (pflash 0.6B), scores from `kvflash_history_` token IDs so `reselect` can page evicted chunks back
87	  (the memory lever). Adaptive τ keeps rescore ~12% (qwen35_backend.cpp:1361-1366).
88	- Pinning (additive, no behavior change when unused) in `kvflash_pager.h`: `pinned_` vector +
89	  `pin_chunk/unpin_chunk/is_pinned/pin_range(tok_lo,tok_hi)`. OR-in `is_pinned(c)` to the protection
90	  predicate at BOTH `:329-332` (eviction) and `:293-294` (reselect). Extend `min_pool_tokens` (75-77):
91	  `sink + tail + pinned + 2 ≤ n_blocks` — refuse+log a pin that would deadlock (best-effort, not a
92	  correctness contract; drafter still recalls unpinned).
93	- Backend tags: pin the tool-def prefix span every turn (claude-code resends `tools=` each turn) —
94	  reuse `req.stall_tool_prefix_tokens` if it already marks the tool-prefix length → `pin_range(0, N)`.
95	  Re-apply pins after each prefill rebuild (where `kvflash_history_` is reassigned). Gate/bench: env
96	  `DFLASH_KVFLASH_PIN_SPANS="lo:hi,..."` to pin the known needle deterministically.
97	- Composition (turn 1 pooled prefill → pooled decode → pooled snapshot; turn 2+ pooled restore →
98	  chunked delta-prefill → pooled decode). Confirm verify_width ≤ one chunk so per-batch alloc never
99	  deadlocks.
100	
101	Gates: G3.1 3-turn 128K deterministic + flat VRAM; G3.2 cross-turn needle recall post-restore;
102	G3.3 spec-decode vs force-AR identical greedy (temp 0); G3.4 50-turn loop never trips `slot_for<0`,
103	host-store bounded.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## THE 128K QUALITY GATE (merge gate — ship/no-ship)
108	
109	Single binary, all arms, under `flock /tmp/dflash_gpu.lock`. Config-gate before GPU spend: assert
110	binary md5, grep startup for `[kvflash] resident pool` + policy line, confirm pool + pin spans parsed.
111	
112	Arms: **CTRL** (full KV, no pooling) · **A** (FlowKV/pflash incumbent) · **B** (KVFlash + drafter +
113	pinning — GATES SHIP) · **C** (KVFlash + QK + pinning — non-gating fast-follow). Pool = the residency
114	that fits 128K (report %).
115	
116	Workloads at 128K / ≥117K:
117	- **W1 source-dropped-fact recall (decisive):** fact stated ONCE early (depth 10% and 50%), queried
118	  100K+ tokens later, never re-emitted. Build a "drop" variant of `optimizations/pflash/tests/niah_gen.py`;
119	  grade via `bench_niah_cpp.py` exact-match. **N≥5 seeds** (June-13 verdict flipped at N=1).
120	- **W2 NIAH grid:** depths {10,50,90}% × residency, n=10/cell (RESULTS methodology).
121	- **W3 agentic tool-call integrity:** real claude-code via `harness/clients/run_claude_code.sh`
122	  (`MAX_CTX=131072`, real toolset), 7–9 turn trace growing past 100K; grade tool_valid fraction.
123	
124	Report all three speeds (wall + prefill_TPS + decode_TPS) + recall + tool_valid + KV-VRAM, per arm.
125	
126	B ships only if ALL: (1) W1 recall ≥ CTRL, B ≥ 4/5 at depth-10%; (2) W2 ≥ 88%/cell; (3) W3 tool_valid
127	≥ 0.85; (4) decode_TPS ≥ CTRL and wall ≤ 1.2× A; (5) KV-VRAM ≤ 10% of CTRL.
128	
129	Kill-criteria (NO-SHIP): K1 recall hole pinning can't close at fit-128K residency; K2 tool_valid <0.85
130	even with tool-def pinning; K3 decode slower than CTRL (VRAM win alone insufficient on KV-light hybrid);
131	K4 drafter rescore >20% of decode wall at 128K; K5 W1 pass-rate variance >1/5 at fixed seed. If only C
132	(QK) fails while B passes → not a kill; ship B, QK stays a documented fast-follow.
133	
134	---
135	
136	## Files to change
137	
138	- `server/src/qwen35moe/qwen35moe_backend.cpp` — remove hard-errors (777-785, 1401-1409), `kvf_paged`
139	  chunk-loop driver, pooled `snapshot_save` override, pooled restore path, tool-prefix pin call.
140	- `server/src/common/kvflash_pager.h` — NEW `serialize`/`deserialize` + `for_each_segment`; pinning API
141	  + extend protection (293-294, 329-332); deadlock floor (75-77).
142	- `server/src/qwen35/internal.h` — `PrefixSnapshot` { `kvflash_blob`, `is_pooled` }.
143	- `server/src/qwen35/qwen35_target_graph.cpp` — `skip_kv` flag on snapshot/restore_target_cache.
144	- `server/src/qwen35/qwen35_backend.cpp` — pin tool-def span wiring; (snapshot_save guard if lifting to base).
145	- Bench: `optimizations/pflash/tests/niah_gen.py` (drop variant) + `bench_niah_cpp.py`; `harness/clients/run_claude_code.sh`.
146	
147	## Reuse (do not rewrite)
148	
149	`hybrid_forward_batch` (whole pooled-prefill body), `build_layer_prefn_step(kvflash)`,
150	`build_full_attn_block(kv_write_rows)`, `slot_for/alloc_span/zero_free_blocks/reselect`,
151	`pipelined_decode_one_token(kv_slot)`, `snapshot/restore_target_cache` SSM/conv paths, the dense
152	`do_prefill` mask/positions recipe as spec, the drafter scorer, the restore residual-loop seam (53f63767).
153	
154	## Risks
155	
156	RoPE/DeltaNet continuity (logical positions + contiguous non-overlapping chunks; gate G2.2/G3.2);
157	maskless-decode contract (zeroed free slots; G1.3); MoE routing under paging (exact mask → identical
158	routing; G1.2 with cold experts); 128K blob size (disk-cache, not VRAM); async paging OUT OF SCOPE
159	(synchronous, speed-only). Build on WSL2: C++-mostly, per-TU recompile + relink; submodule pinned at
160	`9cd9e1ed` (= main); use `DFLASH_SERVER_BIN=<worktree>` until merged.
161	
162	## Verification / how to run
163	
164	Per-phase: build (cmake --build build --target dflash_server) → run the phase's temp-0 bit-identity
165	gate (cold full-prefill vs paged, token-for-token, via a clean harness like the session's
166	verify_restore pattern but using `harness/clients/run_claude_code.sh` for agentic). Final: the 128K
167	quality gate (W1/W2/W3, N≥5) with the four arms. Verify each gate GREEN before the next phase.
168	
169	## Ultracode execution structure (next session)
170	
171	Phase the workflow: (1) Phase-1 implement+build+G1 gates; (2) Phase-2 implement+build+G2; (3) Phase-3
172	implement+build+G3; (4) the 128K merge gate (4 arms × W1/W2/W3). Each phase = a pipeline stage with its
173	bit-identity gate as a hard barrier (do not proceed on a failed gate). Commit per phase (no attribution;
174	`DFLASH_SERVER_BIN=<worktree>` for benches). One GPU job at a time (flock). Report all three speeds.
175

This plan is a multi-phase, single-GPU, deeply-coupled C++ implementation gated phase-by-phase on bit-identity benches. Before writing a single line of CUDA on assumptions a prior session wrote down, I verify the load-bearing facts against the current tree — line numbers drift, and my standing rules say bench/build the *shipping* tree, not a remembered one. That verification is genuinely parallel (independent read-only checks), so it's the right thing to fan out. The implementation itself is sequential and funnels through one 3090 — I'll drive that single-lane behind the gates, not as a parallel code fan-out.

Launching the pre-flight verification sweep now.

Now I have a complete picture. Here is the tight report.

---

**1. BACKEND DISPATCH IN test_kvflash — VERDICT: MOE-CAPABLE**

`test_kvflash.cpp` calls `load_target_gguf(argv[1], backend, w)` then `build_qwen35_graph(ctx, gf, *w, *cache, gi)`. The loader in `server/src/qwen35/gguf_target_loader.cpp` reads the GGUF `general.architecture` key and sets `is_moe = (arch_str == "qwen35moe")`. The Q3_K_M file reports `qwen35moe` in its header. `TargetWeights::is_moe` is populated from it, and inside `qwen35_target_graph.cpp` the per-layer dispatch is:

```cpp
ggml_tensor * ffn  = w.is_moe ? build_qwen35moe_ffn(ctx, post, w, L, &moe_selected)
                              : build_swiglu_ffn(ctx, post, L);
```

There is no hardwired arch — the graph builder reads `w.is_moe` at every layer. Passing the Q3_K_M MoE gguf instantiates the MoE FFN path throughout.

There is one important subtlety for the generate-path (not test_kvflash, but relevant to Q4): `Qwen35MoeBackend::generate_impl` checks `if (!target_weights().moe_hybrid)` — if no hybrid cold/hot split is configured, it falls through to `Qwen35Backend::generate_impl`. The Q3_K_M on a fully-GPU-resident run will have `moe_hybrid` populated only if experts don't all fit in VRAM. If they fit, `moe_hybrid` is null and the dense `Qwen35Backend::generate_impl` path runs — but `build_qwen35_graph` still uses `w.is_moe` for the FFN inside each layer's compute graph, so the MoE expert routing is still live.

**2. WHICH FLAGS DRIVE THE GENERATE-PATH POOLED PREFILL**

The pooled chunked prefill (the `kvf_paged` code path added in `qwen35moe_backend.cpp` lines 779-804, and equivalently in `Qwen35Backend::do_prefill` at lines 976-1072) fires when:
```
kvflash_active() && prompt_len > kvflash_tokens_ - kvflash_pager_.chunk_tokens()
```

`kvflash_active()` requires `kvflash_tokens_ > 0`, which is set from `DFLASH_KVFLASH_POOL` env var. The condition means: prompt must exceed `(pool - 64)` tokens. None of `--niah`, `--niah256`, or `--longab` exist in test_kvflash's MoE context — those modes are in test_kvflash itself and they all use `BatchStepper` which is the same pooled chunked loop (`step_chunk`), but over the dense qwen35 weights, not the server-level generate path.

For the G1 gate (forced-paged vs identity on the MoE generate path), none of the test_kvflash flags are relevant. test_kvflash's internal `BatchStepper` calls `build_qwen35_graph` directly and bypasses `generate_impl` entirely. It does exercise the kvflash pager + pooled chunked prefill logic, but only against the qwen35 dense weights as loaded from whatever gguf is passed. The `--prompt=N` + `--pool-c=N` default suite (run A/B/C/F) is what forces the paged path in test_kvflash: Run C uses `pool_c=1024` with default `n_prompt=512` + `n_gen=1200` (total 1712 > 1024). Run F uses `prompt=2048, pool=1024` — this explicitly exercises the pooled chunked prefill (`BatchStepper.step_chunk`) in single-token mode. To push `prompt_len > pool` in test_kvflash: use default args or `--prompt=2048 --pool-c=1024`.

For the **server-level generate_impl MoE path**, the trigger is `DFLASH_KVFLASH_POOL=<N>` where N < prompt_tokens.

**2. WHEN IS `moe_hybrid` ACTIVE — and how to force it**

`moe_hybrid` is populated at the end of `load_target_model` (line 203) **only if** the experts don't all fit. The logic:

1. `load_target_gguf_partial` loads everything except expert tensors onto GPU (line 79).
2. `load_dynamic_placement` computes `expert_budget = gpu_total - core_bytes - kv_total - 200MB_warm - 512MB_safety` (lines 2273-2276).
3. If `placement.total_hot >= n_layer * n_expert` (all experts fit in budget), the code does a **full reload** via `load_target_gguf` at line 113 and **returns immediately without setting `moe_hybrid`**. The resulting `TargetWeights::moe_hybrid` stays null (default `shared_ptr`).
4. If any experts are cold, execution continues to Phase 3 and `out.moe_hybrid = std::move(hybrid)` is set at line 203.

**For Q3_K_M (15.5 GB) on a 24 GB RTX 3090:** non-expert tensors (attention, norms, embed, lm_head) ~5-6 GB + KV cache (depends on `--max-ctx`, e.g. 8192 ctx ≈ 0.7 GB) + 200 MB + 512 MB ≈ ~7 GB consumed, leaving ~17 GB for experts. Q3_K_M expert-only weight ~10-11 GB fits. `total_hot >= n_layer * n_expert` evaluates true. **The full-GPU reload fires, `moe_hybrid` stays null, and your code is skipped.**

**The forcing env var is `DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB`** (line 2284):

```cpp
if (const char * cap_env = std::getenv("DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB")) {
    uint64_t cap_bytes = (uint64_t)std::atoi(cap_env) * 1024ULL * 1024ULL;
    if (cap_bytes > 0 && cap_bytes < expert_budget) {
        expert_budget = cap_bytes;   // artificial cap
    }
}
```

So **yes, pooled MoE prefill via the dense path is already functional for the experts-fit case**. Your Phase-1 edit only matters when `moe_hybrid != null` (cold experts present).

To exercise your chunk loop you need three things simultaneously:
- `moe_hybrid != null` (cold experts forced)
- `kvflash_active()` true (`kvflash_tokens_ > 0`)
- `prompt_len > kvflash_tokens_ - kvflash_pager_.chunk_tokens()`

If 2 GB leaves too few hot experts to function (routing fails or perf degrades badly), raise `DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB` to e.g. 8192 to keep more hot while still leaving some cold. The minimum that guarantees at least one cold expert per layer is any value below `total_expert_bytes / (n_layer * n_expert) * n_layer` — approximately the per-layer cold threshold. **No bigger quant is needed.** Q3_K_M + `DFLASH_EXPERT_BUDGET_MB` is sufficient. No `--moe-*` CLI flag exists for this — the env var is the only lever.

> If any GitNexus tool warns the index is stale, run `npx gitnexus analyze` in terminal first.

## Always Do

- **MUST run impact analysis before editing any symbol.** Before modifying a function, class, or method, run `gitnexus_impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})` and report the blast radius (direct callers, affected processes, risk level) to the user.
- **MUST run `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before committing** to verify your changes only affect expected symbols and execution flows.
- **MUST warn the user** if impact analysis returns HIGH or CRITICAL risk before proceeding with edits.
- When exploring unfamiliar code, use `gitnexus_query({query: "concept"})` to find execution flows instead of grepping. It returns process-grouped results ranked by relevance.
- When you need full context on a specific symbol — callers, callees, which execution flows it participates in — use `gitnexus_context({name: "symbolName"})`.

## Never Do

- NEVER edit a function, class, or method without first running `gitnexus_impact` on it.
- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis.
- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `gitnexus_rename` which understands the call graph.
- NEVER commit changes without running `gitnexus_detect_changes()` to check affected scope.

static std::string generate_id(const char * prefix) {
    static std::atomic<uint64_t> counter{0};
    char buf[64];
    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "%s_%016llx",
                  prefix, (unsigned long long)counter.fetch_add(1));
    return buf;
}

// Logging helpers shared by route_request() / worker_loop(). Kept static
// (file-scope) so they don't leak into the public ABI; the chat lifecycle
// logs that use them are part of #270's request-tracing instrumentation.
static const char * api_format_name(ApiFormat format) {
    switch (format) {
    case ApiFormat::OPENAI_CHAT: return "chat";
    case ApiFormat::ANTHROPIC:   return "anthropic";
    case ApiFormat::RESPONSES:   return "responses";
    default:                     return "unknown";
    }
}

json build_props_body(const ServerConfig & config,
                      const PrefixCache & prefix_cache,
                      const ToolMemory & tool_memory) {
    // arch-gated capabilities (mirrors Python _capabilities()).
    const bool is_qwen = (config.arch.rfind("qwen", 0) == 0);
    const bool reasoning_supported = is_qwen;
    const bool speculative_supported = is_qwen;
    const bool tools_supported = is_qwen;

    auto pcs  = prefix_cache.stats();
    auto pcfs = prefix_cache.full_stats();
    auto tms  = tool_memory.stats();

    const bool pflash_enabled =
        (config.pflash_mode != ServerConfig::PflashMode::OFF);
    // speculative_mode reports the *active* path, not arch capability. A
    // Qwen-family model started without --ddtree has the capability but no
    // active speculative decode, so it must report "off" — otherwise clients
    // see `speculative_mode == "dflash"` paired with `speculative.enabled ==
    // false` and the two contradict (codex review feedback on 8d6ff04).
    std::string speculative_mode;
    if (pflash_enabled)                    speculative_mode = "pflash";
    else if (config.speculative_enabled)   speculative_mode = "dflash";
    else                                   speculative_mode = "off";

    // Spec §4.2: the five-tier vocabulary (low | medium | high | x-high | max)
    // all activate the phase-1 envelope. Advertise the full set when the
    // arch supports reasoning so clients can negotiate the higher tiers.
    json reasoning_efforts = json::array();
    if (reasoning_supported) {
        reasoning_efforts.push_back("low");
        reasoning_efforts.push_back("medium");
        reasoning_efforts.push_back("high");
        reasoning_efforts.push_back("x-high");
        reasoning_efforts.push_back("max");
    }

    json server = {
        {"name",         kServerName},
        {"version",      DFLASH_SERVER_VERSION},
        {"props_schema", kPropsSchema},
    };

    json pflash;
    if (!pflash_enabled) {
        pflash = {
            {"enabled",      false},
            {"mode",         "off"},
            {"threshold",    nullptr},
            {"keep_ratio",   nullptr},
            {"drafter_gguf", nullptr},
            {"skip_park",    nullptr},
            {"bsa_enabled",  nullptr},
            {"bsa_alpha",    nullptr},
            {"lm_head_fix",  nullptr},

        const char * alpha_env = std::getenv("DFLASH_FP_ALPHA");

        json bsa_alpha = nullptr;
        if (alpha_env && *alpha_env) {
            try { bsa_alpha = std::stod(alpha_env); }
            catch (const std::exception &) { bsa_alpha = nullptr; }

        std::string mode_str =
            (config.pflash_mode == ServerConfig::PflashMode::AUTO)   ? "auto"   :
            (config.pflash_mode == ServerConfig::PflashMode::ALWAYS) ? "always" : "off";
        pflash = {
            {"enabled",      true},
            {"mode",         mode_str},
            {"threshold",    config.pflash_threshold},
            {"keep_ratio",   config.pflash_keep_ratio},
            {"drafter_gguf", config.pflash_drafter_path.empty()
                              ? json(nullptr)

    // omits the field — these come from the loaded model card's sampling

                {"supports_top_p",              true},
                {"supports_top_k",              true},

// Normalize Anthropic's `system` field (top-level on /v1/messages and
// /v1/messages/count_tokens) into a leading `{role:"system", content:...}`
// entry on `messages`. Accepts either a flat string or an array of typed
// blocks (`[{type:"text", text:"..."}]`), and strips any
// `x-anthropic-billing-header:`-prefixed block injected by Claude Code so
// it never reaches the model or the token counter.
//
// Side-effect: prepends a system message to `messages` when the body has
// a non-empty `system` field after billing-header filtering. No-op
// otherwise. Both endpoints call this with identical semantics — having
// one helper guarantees token counting and generation can't drift.
static void normalize_anthropic_system(const json & body, json & messages) {
    if (!body.contains("system")) return;
    json sys_content = body["system"];
    if (sys_content.is_array()) {
        json filtered = json::array();
        for (const auto & block : sys_content) {
            if (block.is_object() && block.value("type", "") == "text") {
                std::string text = block.value("text", "");
                if (text.rfind("x-anthropic-billing-header:", 0) == 0) {
                    continue;  // skip Claude Code billing header block
                }
            }
            filtered.push_back(block);
        }
        sys_content = std::move(filtered);
    } else if (sys_content.is_string()) {
        std::string s = sys_content.get<std::string>();
        if (s.rfind("x-anthropic-billing-header:", 0) == 0) {
            sys_content = "";
        }
    }
    if (!sys_content.empty()) {
        json sys_msg = {{"role", "system"}, {"content", sys_content}};
        messages.insert(messages.begin(), sys_msg);
    }
}

json parse_responses_arguments(const json & item) {
    if (!item.contains("arguments")) return json::object();
    const auto & arguments = item["arguments"];
    if (arguments.is_object()) return arguments;
    if (arguments.is_string()) {
        try {
            return json::parse(arguments.get<std::string>());
        } catch (const std::exception &) {
            return json::object();
        }
    }
    return json::object();
}

std::string render_tool_call_xml(const std::string & name, const json & arguments) {
    std::string out = "<function=" + name + ">\n";
    if (arguments.is_object()) {
        for (const auto & [key, value] : arguments.items()) {
            out += "<parameter=" + key + ">\n";
            out += value.is_string() ? value.get<std::string>() : value.dump();
            out += "\n</parameter>\n";
        }
    }
    out += "</function>\n";
    return out;
}

std::vector<ChatMessage> normalize_chat_messages(
    const json & messages,
    ApiFormat format,
    ToolMemory & tool_memory) {
    std::vector<ChatMessage> chat_msgs;
    std::vector<std::string> system_parts;

    if (messages.is_array()) {
        for (const auto & m : messages) {
            if (format == ApiFormat::RESPONSES && m.is_object()) {
                std::string item_type = m.value("type", "message");
                if (item_type == "function_call") {
                    std::string call_id = m.value("call_id", m.value("id", ""));
                    std::string raw;
                    if (!call_id.empty()) {
                        raw = tool_memory.lookup({call_id});
                    }
                    if (raw.empty()) {
                        raw = render_tool_call_xml(m.value("name", ""),
                                                   parse_responses_arguments(m));
                    }
                    chat_msgs.push_back({"assistant", raw});
                    continue;
                }
                if (item_type == "function_call_output") {
                    std::string output;
                    if (m.contains("output") && m["output"].is_string()) {
                        output = m["output"].get<std::string>();
                    } else if (m.contains("output")) {
                        output = m["output"].dump();
                    }
                    chat_msgs.push_back({"tool", output,
                                         m.value("call_id", m.value("id", ""))});
                    continue;
                }
            }

            ChatMessage cm;
            cm.role = m.value("role", "user");

            bool replayed = false;
            if (cm.role == "assistant" && m.contains("tool_calls") &&
                m["tool_calls"].is_array() && !m["tool_calls"].empty()) {
                std::vector<std::string> call_ids;
                for (const auto & tc : m["tool_calls"]) {
                    std::string id = tc.value("id", "");
                    if (!id.empty()) call_ids.push_back(id);
                }
                std::string raw = tool_memory.lookup(call_ids);
                if (!raw.empty()) {
                    cm.content = raw;
                    replayed = true;
                }
            }

            if (!replayed) {
                if (m.contains("content") && m["content"].is_string()) {
                    cm.content = m["content"].get<std::string>();
                } else if (m.contains("content") && m["content"].is_array()) {
                    for (const auto & part : m["content"]) {
                        std::string ptype = part.value("type", "");
                        if (ptype == "text" || ptype == "input_text" ||
                            ptype == "output_text") {
                            cm.content += part.value("text", "");
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            if (format == ApiFormat::RESPONSES &&
                (cm.role == "system" || cm.role == "developer")) {
                system_parts.push_back(cm.content);
            } else {
                chat_msgs.push_back(std::move(cm));
            }
        }
    } else if (messages.is_string()) {
        chat_msgs.push_back({"user", messages.get<std::string>()});
    }

    if (!system_parts.empty()) {
        std::string merged_system;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < system_parts.size(); i++) {
            if (i) merged_system += "\n\n";
            merged_system += system_parts[i];
        }
        chat_msgs.insert(chat_msgs.begin(), {"system", merged_system});
    }

    return chat_msgs;
}

                       const ServerConfig & config)

    , prefix_cache_(config.prefix_cache_cap, tokenizer)

{
